strategyPoints: Tire wear will be a major factor on this abrasive surface. Managing the rubber will be key to a successful race on this 6.172km configuration.
The long pit lane here at Bathurst means the pit window is longer than at other circuits. Teams will need to factor that into their strategy calculations.
Fuel consumption is always a concern at Bathurst. Teams will be carefully monitoring their fuel levels to avoid running dry on the final lap.
Safety cars are almost guaranteed at Bathurst. Teams need to be prepared to react quickly to changing track conditions and adjust their strategy accordingly.
The optimum pit stop strategy will likely be a two-stopper, but a well-timed safety car could throw everything into disarray.
With such a long lap, getting stuck behind a slower car can cost a significant amount of time. Overtaking opportunities are crucial.
The heat will take its toll on both the cars and the drivers. Hydration and cooling are essential for a long and grueling race.
Track position is vital at Bathurst. Overtaking is difficult, so getting a good start and maintaining your position is crucial.
